nodes.description: Owner address state variable, initialized to address(0).
Boolean lock state var used to guard bet().
Payable bet function that pays out 2 ether on a pseudo-random win.
Owner-only function setting locked to true.
Owner-only function setting locked to false.
Assigns gameOwner, callable when owner is zero address or caller is owner.
Owner-only function transferring amount ether to msg.sender.
View pseudo-random generator using block.timestamp and block.difficulty.
Payable fallback that forwards to bet().
Caller-controlled address used for ownership checks and as call/transfer target.
Miner-influenced timestamp used as randomness seed.
Low-level msg.sender.call.value(2 ether)() executed before state is finalized, enabling reentrancy.
Multiplication amount * (1 ether) that can overflow in Solidity 0.4.x.
Parameter of own(address) used to set the new gameOwner.
Parameter of releaseFunds(uint) scaled by 1 ether before transfer.

edges.reason: lock() reads gameOwner to authorize the caller.
unlock() reads gameOwner to authorize the caller.
own() reads gameOwner to decide whether reassignment is allowed.
releaseFunds() reads gameOwner to authorize the transfer.
bet() reads the locked flag to guard the payout path.
bet() performs an external low-level call to msg.sender before resolving state, enabling reentrancy.
lock() writes locked = true.
unlock() writes locked = false.
own() writes the gameOwner state variable.
releaseFunds() forwards the scaled amount into the transfer.
bet() uses random() derived from miner-influenced values to decide the payout.
The fallback function invokes bet().
msg.sender is compared to gameOwner in lock().
msg.sender is compared to gameOwner in unlock().
msg.sender is used to authorize ownership change in own().
msg.sender is checked and receives funds in releaseFunds().
The external call target is the untrusted msg.sender.
random() depends on block.timestamp, making outcome miner-manipulable.
The ether-sending call can re-enter the contract via its payable fallback.
The unchecked multiplication result feeds the transfer amount.
The owner parameter becomes the new privileged gameOwner.
The unvalidated amount parameter determines the transferred value.
The amount parameter is multiplied by 1 ether without overflow checks.

normalization_plan.reason: The owner parameter only exists to set gameOwner inside own() and has no independent security role.
The amount parameter is only used inside releaseFunds() to compute the transfer value and can be merged into that core function.
